result.topic_en: Euler derives the conditions under which two surfaces given by coordinate integrals in two variables r and s are applicable (isometric) to each other, parametrises the solution by angles, and remarks that such surfaces extend to infinity, so a closed surface like a sphere cannot be represented this way and closed figures admit no deformation.

Adnotatio. Probe autem notari convenit hic alteram superficiem non pro data assumi licere, saltem non patet quomodo functiones $p$, $m$ et $n$ assumi debeant, ut prior superficies datam obtineat figuram v. g. sphaericam. Cum enim in utrisque formulis binae variabiles $r$ et $s$ in infinitum augeri queant, facile patet utramque superficiem necessario in infinitum protendi, neque hanc extensionem per quaepiam imaginaria tolli posse. Quamobrem figura sphaerica neque ulla alia figura in spatio finito subsistens in his formulis contenta esse potest. Quod autem ad figuras terminatas seu undique clausas attinet, judicium de iis aliter instituendum videtur. Statim enim atque figura solida undique est clausa, nullam amplius mutationem patitur; quemadmodum ex notis illis figuris corporeis, quae corpora regularia vocari solent, intelligere licet. items.quote: saltem non patet quomodo functiones $p$, $m$ et $n$ assumi debeant, ut prior superficies datam obtineat figuram v. g. sphaericam.
items.english: at least it is not clear how the functions p, m and n should be chosen so that the first surface obtains a given shape, e.g. spherical.

items.quote: Quamobrem figura sphaerica neque ulla alia figura in spatio finito subsistens in his formulis contenta esse potest.
items.english: Therefore neither the spherical figure nor any other figure confined to a finite space can be contained in these formulas.

items.quote: Statim enim atque figura solida undique est clausa, nullam amplius mutationem patitur
items.english: For as soon as a solid figure is closed on all sides, it admits no further change.

items.quote: Unde quatenus superficies sphaerica est integra, nullam mutationem admittit.
items.english: Hence, insofar as the spherical surface is complete, it admits no change.
